summary: A modular monolith build: Server-rendered HTML + HTMX on the frontend, C# + ASP.NET Core for the backend, Microsoft SQL Server for data, hosted on Azure App Service / Container Apps. About $44-375 a month. With 2 engineer(s), one deployable with strict internal module boundaries is the fastest and cheapest to run; modules can be extracted into services later.

frontend.justification: Server-rendered HTML + HTMX is the frontend for an Internal tool / admin panel project with about 300 daily users (~1.6 requests/s at peak), built by a team of 2 in 6 weeks. Its strongest weighted criterion for your answers is low ops burden: 5.0/5 at weight 4.0, the largest share of its score. It leads the runner-up, React SPA (Vite), by 1.4 stack points (points of the overall stack score, the average of the four layer scores).

alternatives.why_not: Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 1.4 points. Server-rendered HTML + HTMX is stronger on team skill match (4.5 vs 3.5), learning curve (5.0 vs 4.0); React SPA (Vite) is stronger on ecosystem maturity (5.0 vs 3.0), rich client interactivity (5.0 vs 2.0).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 3.2 points. Server-rendered HTML + HTMX is stronger on learning curve (5.0 vs 3.0), low ops burden (5.0 vs 4.0); Next.js (React) is stronger on development speed (5.0 vs 4.0), ecosystem maturity (5.0 vs 3.0); Next.js (React) takes a penalty: No search visibility needed: server rendering adds a Node.js server for pages that React SPA (Vite) serves as static files.
Ruled out: Mobile toolkit; web is a target, so the primary frontend is a web framework (mobile app suggested as companion)
Ruled out: Mobile toolkit; web is a target, so the primary frontend is a web framework (mobile app suggested as companion)

tradeoffs: Structure for large teams is only 2.0/5 (weight 1.0).
Rich client interactions (drag-drop editors, offline) get awkward
Requires a server-rendering backend; does not pair with BaaS

backend.justification: C# + ASP.NET Core serves the API at about 1.6 requests/s at peak (Small (50-500 users online at once)) for a team of 2. It runs as a long-running C#/.NET service, so background jobs, WebSockets and database connection pools live in one deployable process. It leads the runner-up, PHP + Laravel, by 3.7 stack points.

alternatives.why_not: Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 3.7 points. C# + ASP.NET Core is stronger on team skill match (4.5 vs 3.5), learning curve (5.0 vs 4.0); PHP + Laravel is stronger on development speed (5.0 vs 4.0); PHP + Laravel takes a penalty: Company-account sign-in (SSO) needs an identity broker such as Keycloak that you run beside this backend.

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 5.1 points. C# + ASP.NET Core is stronger on structure for large teams (5.0 vs 1.0), performance / latency (5.0 vs 3.0); Node.js + Express is stronger on hiring pool (5.0 vs 4.0); Node.js + Express takes a penalty: Company-account sign-in (SSO) needs an identity broker such as Keycloak that you run beside this backend.

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 7.8 points. C# + ASP.NET Core is stronger on team skill match (4.5 vs 1.5), learning curve (5.0 vs 4.0); Python + Django is stronger on development speed (5.0 vs 4.0); Python + Django takes a penalty: Nobody on the team listed Python or a closely related skill: a new server language to learn.
Ruled out: Not on Azure, the cloud you require; No ISO/IEC 27001 certification published

Company-account sign-in (SSO) needs an identity broker such as Keycloak that you run beside this backend (-3).

database.choice: Microsoft SQL Server: Azure SQL Database (General Purpose, serverless or provisioned)
database.justification: Your data is mainly relational and reaches about 20 GB within 12 months; Microsoft SQL Server fits relational data 5/5. You need strong consistency, and Microsoft SQL Server gives it: a read after a write always sees that write. Its share of the estimated bill is $22-$225 a month, against a total budget of $300 a month. It leads the runner-up, PostgreSQL, by 2.2 stack points.

alternatives.why_not: Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 2.2 points. PostgreSQL is stronger on portability (low lock-in) (5.0 vs 3.0), cost at your scale (4.7 vs 4.4).
Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 2.2 points. MySQL is stronger on portability (low lock-in) (5.0 vs 3.0), cost at your scale (4.7 vs 4.4).

Swapping it in lowers the stack score by 12.1 points. Microsoft SQL Server is stronger on data-model fit (5.0 vs 2.0), consistency fit (5.0 vs 3.5); MongoDB is stronger on scalability (5.0 vs 4.0), cost at your scale (4.7 vs 4.4); MongoDB takes a penalty: Only 2/5 fit for your primary 'relational' data.
Ruled out: Not on Azure, the cloud you require

tradeoffs: Commercial licence: managed instances cost more than PostgreSQL or MySQL of the same size
T-SQL and its features are specific to SQL Server, so moving off it is a migration

hosting.choice: Azure App Service / Container Apps, region Central India (Pune)
hosting.justification: Azure App Service / Container Apps hosts the stack for users in India at a 99.9% availability target. It runs the C# + ASP.NET Core API as long-running processes, sized for ~1.6 requests/s at peak. It has a region in India, so data can stay in the country. Its share of the estimated bill is $22-$150 a month, against a total budget of $300 a month.

supporting.choice: Microsoft Entra ID (existing), signed in through OpenID Connect
supporting.justification: infrastructure.existing_systems lists Microsoft Entra ID: users sign in with the accounts it already manages, so there is no new user store, MFA and password rules come from it, and removing someone there removes their access here.

alternatives.choice: Keycloak self-hosted in your Indian region, or framework built-in auth
alternatives.why_not: A second identity system to run beside Microsoft Entra ID, which already holds the users

alternatives.why_not: A second identity system to run beside Microsoft Entra ID, which already holds the users

tradeoffs: Sign-in depends on Microsoft Entra ID being reachable

supporting.choice: OpenTelemetry instrumentation -> Azure Monitor / App Insights
supporting.justification: Traces, metrics and error tracking from day one; required to defend an availability target.
